pattern/one: To measure a slope, take a tiny step, h, and divide the rise by it. For x squared at x equals one, the slope comes out as two.
pattern/every: But that is the slope at one point only. Is there a way to know it at every point at once?
pattern/slide: Slide the tangent along the curve, and mark each slope it measures on a second graph below, at the same x.
pattern/line: The marks fall on a straight line: at every x, the slope is two times x. So the derivative of x squared is two x, everywhere at once.
pattern/cube: Do the same for x cubed. This time the slopes trace a curve: three x squared.
pattern/check: Check one point. At x equals two, the measured slope is twelve, and three times two squared is twelve.
rule/power: x squared means x times x. The small raised two counts how many x's are multiplied, and it is called the power.
rule/sq: x squared becomes two x, where the arrow reads “becomes”. The two came down in front, and the power dropped by one, leaving plain x.
rule/cube: x cubed became three x squared: the three came down, and the power fell by one, leaving x squared.
rule/rule: The same holds for any power n: x to the n becomes n times x to the n minus one. That is the power rule: the rule for the derivative of a power.
sums/factor: A number multiplying a power comes along for the ride. Five x cubed becomes five times three x squared: fifteen x squared.
sums/sum: Taking a derivative is also called differentiating. A sum is differentiated one piece at a time. The next piece, two x, is a straight line with slope two.
sums/zero: A constant on its own is flat, so its derivative is zero. The seven drops out.
sums/whole: So five x cubed plus two x plus seven has derivative fifteen x squared plus two.
sums/ask: Now the slope at one point. For that f, what is f prime of two?
sums/put: Put two in for x. Fifteen times two squared is sixty.
sums/add: Then add the two from the line: sixty-two.
